examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Write a probability tree for hits/misses. AMAT may use incremental miss penalties or total end-to-end times; mixing those conventions double-counts earlier lookups. CPU time depends on instruction count, CPI and clock period. For multicore speedup, include serial work and explicitly stated per-core overhead rather than using ideal Amdahl scaling alone.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
L1 time is 2 ns, miss rate 0.1. An L1 miss adds 10 ns; a conditional L2 miss rate 0.2 adds a further 100 ns. Find AMAT in ns.

**Answer: 5.** AMAT=2+0.1(10+0.2·100)=2+3=5 ns. L2 misses occur on 0.1·0.2=0.02 of all references, not 0.2 of all references.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A local L2 miss rate is conditional on reaching L2. A global miss rate already includes earlier cache outcomes and must not be multiplied again.

Do not double-count lookup time if a question gives total miss time instead of additional miss penalty.
